_doc: Declarative device tuning the SuperApp applies through its OWN shell channel (uid 2000, the embedded adb client / libs:shizuku-adb-debug-tools ladder). Every entry is {id, title, why, apply[], verify{cmd, expect}}. The engine (app/.../system/DeviceTuning.kt) runs verify first, applies ONLY the entries whose verify output differs from expect, re-verifies, and records APPLIED / PENDING (no shell yet) / FAILED per entry. Nothing here is hardcoded in Kotlin — add an entry, ship, done. Baked into BuildConfig.DEVICE_TUNING_B64 by app/build.gradle (compact, _doc keys stripped).
_doc_phantom: Android 12+ ships a 'phantom process killer': at most 32 child processes (forked by apps, not by zygote) may exist system-wide, and any background child using 'excessive CPU' is SIGKILLed. On this Android 14 phone that is what ends the Cloud Terminal proot sessions with '[Process completed (signal 9)]' — memory is NOT the cause. The fix Termux documents needs shell uid: disable the monitor and lift the cap. Both are persistent settings; device_config additionally needs sync disabled or Google's remote config overwrites max_phantom_processes.

entries.title: Phantom monitor off
entries.why: Android 12+ kills background child processes (proot, sshd, tmux) on 'excessive CPU' and past 32 of them system-wide — the signal-9 behind terminal sessions dying. This turns the monitor off.

entries.title: Phantom process cap
entries.why: Belt and braces with the monitor switch: the system-wide cap of 32 phantom processes is lifted to MAX_INT, and device_config sync is pinned so Google's remote flags do not put the cap back.

entries.title: Cached-apps freezer off
entries.why: Android 11+ freezes (SIGSTOPs) every process of an app the moment it is cached — a Claude session in the terminal stops dead while another app is in front and resumes only when the terminal is back (the owner sees it as a hang). Applied at next boot (activity_manager_native_boot namespace).

entries.title: Fleet apps exempt from doze and background network restriction
entries.why: Doze (DOZE chain) and Android 15's background network restriction (APP_BACKGROUND chain) cut the network of every app that is not in the foreground: netpolicy showed the Store in procState CAC with effective=DOZE|APP_BACKGROUND, every download it ran after the user switched away failed at the resolver ("network DNS none"). The power-save allowlist (the same thing Settings → Battery → Unrestricted grants) lifts both chains: allowed=POWER_SAVE_ALLOWLIST|POWER_SAVE_EXCEPT_IDLE_ALLOWLIST, effective=NONE. Declared for every fleet app that works in the background.

entries.title: Terminals in the active standby bucket
entries.why: An app in a restricted standby bucket gets its jobs, alarms and network deferred; the terminals stay active so a session keeps its network while in the background. A bucket of 5 (EXEMPTED, after the doze whitelist) or 10 (ACTIVE) both satisfy it.

entries.title: Mesh engine holds the VPN consent
entries.why: Android grants VPN consent per package (VpnService.prepare), and only the package that owns the service can ask: the WireGuard engine lib (com.diegonmarcos.cloudlib.netwg), not the apps that drive it. Granted here, the Account's mesh apply and the fleet API bring the tunnel up with no dialog a terminal cannot answer; the engine's row under Settings › VPN is this grant. The SuperApp's own firewall VpnServices keep asking through the system dialog when the firewall is first enabled — nothing grants those.

verify.cmd: appops get com.diegonmarcos.cloudlib.netwg ACTIVATE_VPN | grep -q allow && echo ok

entries.title: Android Private DNS off
entries.why: Android's Automatic Private DNS validates DNS-over-TLS against the public servers the VPN carries (1.1.1.1, dns.google) and then sends EVERY lookup to them over DoT before any plain server is asked — the fleet resolver (hickory at 10.0.0.1) is never reached, so vault.diegonmarcos.com answers its public address even with the mesh up. Off makes the resolver ask the VPN's servers in their declared order, fleet first (ui.dns.android_private_dns.private_presets_require).
